entries.proposition: 🔴 THIS ADJUDICATES THE INTERNAL CONTRADICTION THIS ACTOR COULD NOT SETTLE ON PMID 25245215 EARLIER IN THE SAME WAVE, AND IT SETTLES IT AGAINST BOTH HALVES. Chapter 8 (PMID 25245215) states in one section that 'WWOX ablation results in growth retardation' and four sections later that 'Wwox-deficient mice develop normally', citing reference [7] for both. This 2010 review — with Aqeilan as a shared author and citing the same primary sources [6-8] — gives the phenotype with the precision both later sentences lose: mice are indistinguishable from littermates AT BIRTH, are SMALLER BY DAY 3, and are all dead by 4 weeks. So 'develop normally' is true only of birth and false by day 3, and 'growth retardation' is true but postnatal in onset rather than developmental. NEITHER of chapter 8's two sentences is accurate on its own, and the disagreement between them is a compression artefact, not a dispute about data. The corpus cross-query on 17360458 could not reach this because that reading carried no growth statement; a second document did.
entries.snippet: At birth, homozygous Wwox-deficient (Wwox−/−) pups were indistinguishable from wild-type (WT) or heterozygous littermates; at 3 days, homozygous pups were smaller than littermates and all Wwox−/− mice died by 4 weeks after birth with severe metabolic defects

entries.proposition: THE SPECIFIC GROWTH PHENOTYPE, WHICH IS SKELETAL AND ORGAN-LEVEL RATHER THAN GLOBAL. Recorded beside the preceding locator because it is the datum chapter 8's phrase 'growth retardation' compresses.
entries.snippet: Macroscopic and histological examination of the organs confirmed atrophy of organs, gonadal abnormalities and bone growth retardation in Wwox−/− mice

entries.proposition: 🔴 AN EXPLICIT FAILURE TO REPLICATE, STATED BY THE AUTHORS ABOUT ANOTHER GROUP'S RESULT — AND ITS CAVEAT IS PRESENT IN CHAPTER 8'S PROSE AND ABSENT FROM CHAPTER 8'S TABLE. These authors could not reproduce WWOX-p53 binding under the conditions where WWOX-p73 binding was reproducible. PMID 25245215's Table 1 lists TP53 as a WWOX partner with readout 'Promotes apoptosis' and NO caveat, while its running text does carry the qualification. That matters because a partner TABLE is exactly the surface a downstream consumer mines, and the table is where the negative disappears. A repository building an interactome from Table 1 alone would record an unqualified WWOX-p53 interaction that neither this paper nor chapter 8's own prose supports.
entries.snippet: we were unable to recapitulate p53 binding to Wwox reported by another group

entries.proposition: 🔴 A DIRECT REVERSAL OF DIRECTION BETWEEN THE TWO DOCUMENTS READ IN THIS WAVE, AND THE LATER ONE RESTS THE NEW DIRECTION PARTLY ON UNPUBLISHED DATA. Here in 2010: WWOX expression is REDUCED following UV. In PMID 25245215 (2014): 'our recent results demonstrate that WWOX expression is INCREASED immediately after IR and UV (unpublished data)', introduced by that chapter's own admission that 'Conflicting results were reported on WWOX expression upon exposure to DNA damage'. Aqeilan is an author of both. The 2014 chapter needs the increase for its DDR model, in which WWOX is induced by damage and translocates to the nucleus. Recorded as a directional conflict between two secondary sources with a shared author, NOT as a finding about the biology: neither document measures it, and the primary sources on both sides are unread here.
entries.snippet: Wwox expression is reportedly reduced following UV radiation
entries.anchor: Body, 'Wwox associates with Jun following UV irradiation', final sentence

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE AUTHORS ARGUE AGAINST THEIR OWN THESIS, EXPLICITLY, AND THIS IS THE MOST BALANCED TREATMENT OF THE PASSENGER/DRIVER QUESTION IN THIS ACTOR'S ENTIRE LOT. Three documents in this lot address passenger-versus-driver: PMID 27551470 frames it as a live controversy, PMID 25245215 argues against passenger status in its Introduction and calls it debated in its Conclusion, and THIS one states a concrete mechanism by which the passenger reading could be RIGHT — intron-only deletions that never touch coding sequence — and attributes it to the fragile genes' own architecture. An author-stated argument against the author's own position is the rarest thing in a review layer and is weighted accordingly.
entries.snippet: so that some replication stress-induced small deletions may fall entirely within introns, as has been observed for the FHIT locus, and may not contribute to clonal expansion, supporting arguments against a tumor suppressor role for fragile gene products

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND IT NAMES THE EXPERIMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT — WHICH MAKES THIS A DATED, CHECKABLE OPEN QUESTION RATHER THAN A HEDGE. Delineating WWOX deletion end points would establish whether intron-only deletions occur. Note what this implies for the reference genotype: the question is about SOMATIC deletion architecture in cancer, and answering it either way says nothing about a germline coding variant. Recorded as the concrete revival trigger this document supplies, and as the thing to check against any later fragile-site literature.
entries.snippet: The WWOX locus has thus far not been examined in enough detail to precisely delineate deletion end points and will require further investigation to determine if such intron-only deletions occur.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE SHARPEST QUALIFICATION THIS READING MAKES TO THIS ACTOR'S OWN THREE PRIOR MEASUREMENTS OF THE ABSENCE. This document DOES bring inherited human syndromes into a fragile-site discussion — Bloom's syndrome and Fanconi anemia, at length, with FANCD2 and FANCI at common fragile site loci. So the CFS literature is not closed to constitutional human disease in principle. What it admits is the CANCER-PREDISPOSING kind. That is a strictly sharper statement than 'this literature omits human genetic disorders', which is what the rare/common taxonomy alone supported, and it is available only because this paper was read.
entries.snippet: Bloom's syndrome and Fanconi anemia are inherited syndromes associated with extreme susceptibility to cancer development, through mechanisms that have not been defined in detail.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE TERM SCREEN, WITH ITS DENOMINATOR AND WITH THE ONE THING THAT STOPS IT COUNTING AS A FOURTH INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION. Screened over the 29,965-character article body: epilep 0, seizure 0, brain 0, CNS 0, WOREE 0, encephalopath 0, ataxia 0, intellectual 0, recessive 0, germline 0, neuro 0 — ELEVEN OF TWELVE LITERALLY ZERO, and 'syndrome' occurs 4 times, ALL FOUR being Bloom's syndrome or Fanconi anemia. 🔴 BUT THIS MEASUREMENT CARRIES MUCH LESS WEIGHT THAN THE THREE BEFORE IT AND THE READING SAYS SO RATHER THAN BANKING IT: this article is FEBRUARY 2010, which PREDATES the description of WWOX germline disease. There was no phenotype to omit. Chapter 8 (December 2014) had one and omitted it; this paper could not have included it. Recorded as a chronological control on the earlier measurements, not as a fourth confirmation of them.

entries.proposition: THE COOPERATION QUESTION, AND WHY CHAPTER 8'S 2014 'YET TO BE DETERMINED' IS NARROWER THAN IT READS. In 2010 a retroviral insertion screen is already cited as suggesting that WWOX inactivation cooperates with classical tumour-suppressor loss. Chapter 8 in 2014 says whether TARGETED DELETION of Wwox cooperates with loss of other tumour suppressors 'is yet to be determined'. 🔴 STATED CAREFULLY BECAUSE THE OVERCLAIM IS AVAILABLE AND WOULD BE WRONG: these are not the same claim. An insertional-mutagenesis screen is not a targeted-deletion cross, so the two statements are COMPATIBLE and chapter 8's qualifier is doing real work. What is recorded is only that the cooperation idea was already evidenced by a different design four years earlier, so the later 'yet to be determined' should not be read as 'no evidence exists'.
entries.snippet: suggesting that Wwox inactivation can cooperate with so called 'classical' tumor suppressor loss in tumor development
entries.anchor: Body, 'Wwox expression in common human cancers', paragraph 3

entries.proposition: HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY IS ASSERTED FROM RETAINED PROTEIN IN THE TUMOURS, AND THE INFERENCE IS THE AUTHORS', NOT A MEASUREMENT. Recorded because haploinsufficiency is a load-bearing concept for any dose-based reasoning about a recessive human allele, and because the evidence offered for it here is immunodetection of retained protein in heterozygote tumours rather than an allelic or quantitative assay.
entries.snippet: These tumors expressed Wwox protein, suggesting that haploinsufficiency of Wwox is cancer predisposing.
entries.anchor: Body, 'Wwox as a tumor suppressor', paragraph 1

entries.proposition: 🔴 A HYPOMORPH DEFINED BY AN ARGUMENT RATHER THAN BY A MEASUREMENT, AND THE AUTHORS SAY SO IN THE SAME SENTENCE. The strain's residual WWOX protein is inferred from the mice being viable — 'some protein must be produced... or these mice would not be normal' — which is reasoning from the phenotype to the molecular state, i.e. exactly the direction that cannot then be used to explain the phenotype. Recorded because this repository reasons about residual-function alleles, and a hypomorph whose residual expression was never detected is a weak anchor for any dose-response argument.
entries.snippet: In this mouse strain, it was difficult to demonstrate expression of Wwox protein, though some protein must be produced in multiple organs or these mice would not be normal.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE SDR DOMAIN IS DECLARED FUNCTIONALLY UNCHARACTERISED IN 2010, AND THAT IS DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO THE REFERENCE GENOTYPE. Every signalling function reviewed here runs through the WW domains; the SDR domain's predicted oxidoreductase role is noted and then left. The reference genotype class includes SDR-domain missense variants, so the field's dedicated interactome review of this period supplies NO mechanistic basis for reasoning about them — the absence is about the domain, not merely about the phenotype, and it is stated by the authors themselves.
entries.snippet: Although Wwox contains an SDR domain that is predicted to be involved in oxidation/reduction processes, Wwox signaling functions examined thus far are mainly determined by interaction of its WW domains with PPxY motifs in its partners.
entries.anchor: Body, 'Wwox WW domains & protein interactions', final sentence
